_comment: The live backlog (docs/guides/agent-protocol.md, 'The task format'); the lead writes it on main. Since 25 November 2026 the product tasks are the 3D quality wave (docs/art/3d-quality/plan.md, section 6 'Phases' and section 7 'Tracks'), started by the owner (CLAUDE.md order 1). Models and efforts follow CLAUDE.md order 7: each task names its model and effort; every task is reviewed by a verifier on Opus 5.5 at effort high before it merges. Tasks of the UI wave are kept below as history. Owner tasks (assigned_to 'owner') are never claimed by an agent.

tasks.resync_reason: Cycle 194, candidate 5a5d5f41: the verifier (Opus 5.5 high) failed the review. The numbers reproduce (defences 36011 = 27461 + 8550, 86 draw calls; heist 85446 = 57712 + 27734), but the split is miscounted. (1) budget_split.gd:95-97: _is_outline matches only paths ending in outline.gdshader and misses law_fx_ink.gdshader, the law FX ink hull (cull_front next_pass, law_fx.gd:383-386), so its passes count as mesh; with it, heist reads 56480 mesh + 28966 outline (plan.md's hand figure), defences mesh is 416 too high. (2) budget_split.gd:31-32: outline = total - without, from frame totals, which include each viewport's shadow-pass primitives (opaque next_pass hulls get FLAG_PASS_SHADOW); 926 shadow-pass outline triangles land in outline on defences (true visible split 27971 mesh + 8040 outline). Take outline as the sum of _view(v) with outlines minus the sum without. (3) budget_split.gd:40-41: 'other views' holds the world views' own shadow-pass triangles (4892 on defences) while the line prints '+0 in shadows'; label shadows as shadows. From the owner (12 November 2026, about 20:00Z, in the overseer session's chat): "Yes, raise it to 4 builders." CLAUDE.md order 3 now sets the cap at four UI builders. It drops back to three on its own while the seven-day bar reads allowed_warning: start no fourth builder then, and let a running fourth one finish its task. Why: at 19:12Z phase 2 had 49.8 hours left before its 14 November 21:00Z stop and 50.5 hours of seeded work, so the pace (1.02 hours of work an hour) had no slack; a fourth builder adds about 0.34. (1) On your next cycle, start a fourth builder if only three run. S1, S2 and S3 run now. AIA waits on AIA-R23, which is not blocking and whose default is that the sheet stands. So the first choice is to restart AIA on P2-AIA-motion-1 under that default: it unblocks P2-K1-motion, P2-AIA-motion-2 and P2-S1-result-2. If AIA cannot take the place, give it to the next open task with no unmet deps whose claims are disjoint from the running tasks (owners.py claims), the longest chain first. (2) Batching, from now (agent-protocol.md, 'Batching'): as soon as two or more tasks are ready at once, merge 2-3 with disjoint claims into one candidate; if it fails, re-check each alone. Do not wait for the 2-hour mark: phase 1's median wait from ready to merged was 2.1 hours. Add M15 to acks when read.

Lesson from UI phase 2 (P2-S2-flow-home, cycle 71). The first check_all on candidate 1e438a19 failed one fixture in tools/test_run_checks.sh ("and makes no worktree and no log") although S2 touches no runner file; the re-run on the same sha passed. Your write-up names the likely cause: the planted and refused test repos have the same tree and the same identity, so two commits made in the same second share a sha. The rule: (1) tools/test_run_checks.sh is yours (no task in flight owns it). Make its two test repos differ, with a distinct author identity, commit time or file in each, so their shas cannot collide; do it yourself between merges or seed a small K1 task for it. Never loosen, skip or delete the fixture. (2) Until that fix is on main, a lone FAIL of that fixture on a candidate that touches no runner file is re-run once on the same sha; a second FAIL is real. (3) Two lessons are past their ack_by and unread because their agents are waiting: deliver M12 to AD and M14 to AIA-2 in the prompt when you next start or resume them, and have them ack it in their status files.

Lesson from UI phase 2 (P2-S1-toon-drop, cycle 74). The wait from ready to merged rated worse for the second push in a row: 3.0h for P2-K1-motion, then 2.7h for the toon drop (ready 23:41, merged 02:21). Three causes, all in the merge queue. At 23:41 three tasks were ready at once with disjoint claims (P2-S3-screenkit ready 22:59, P2-K1-motion ready 22:40, P2-S1-toon-drop ready 23:41), yet they were merged one at a time, against the batching rule you acked as M15. P2-K1-motion's merge reached main at 01:40, 51 minutes after its check passed at 00:49. And the toon drop's first check_all stopped on a read-only cargo lock because it was started inside the candidate's worktree, where client/ext/target is a link; the re-run from the main checkout passed. The rule: (1) As soon as two or more tasks are ready with disjoint claims, merge 2 or 3 of them into one candidate, as agent-protocol.md "Batching" says; if the batch fails, re-check each alone. (2) Merge to main and clear the lock in the same turn the check passes, then lock the next candidate in that turn. (3) Start check_all from the main checkout on the candidate sha, never from inside the candidate's worktree, or give that worktree its own writable CARGO_TARGET_DIR. (4) Add M17 to the acks in status/lead.json.

Lesson from the UI report (Work delivered rated worse two pushes in a row: 1.10, then 1.11 hours of work an hour against 1.2). Builder seats sit empty while a builder's session waits idle on its own request until its lease lapses: S2 from about 01:10 to its restart at 02:43 on 13 November, and AIA idle on AIA-R25 until its lease lapsed at 04:43. The rule: each cycle, check every builder's session with get_session. When a session is not working (status_bucket other than working) and has its own request pending, apply that request's default early (as M15 allows) and resume that same session with send_message, or restart it on the same task, without waiting for the lease to lapse.
